question: Should OpenClaw ship and maintain the bundled agent-authored custom-widget execution boundary after the concrete authorization, prompt, and lifecycle defects are repaired?
rationale: The unauthenticated asset route, persisted approval state, sandboxed iframe, and parent-mediated data/prompt bridge intentionally establish a repository-level security boundary that automation cannot accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Ship after hardening
options.body: Fix all current-head blockers, add diagnostic lifecycle proof, and obtain explicit security-owner approval for the bundled boundary.

options.title: Land trusted widgets only
options.body: Keep durable Workspaces, built-in widgets, CLI, and tools while removing custom-widget asset serving and bridge capabilities.

options.title: Pause the landing
options.body: Keep the canonical tracking issue open but decline this branch until the custom-code boundary is narrowed or redesigned.

recommendation.title: Ship after hardening
recommendation.body: Fix all current-head blockers, add diagnostic lifecycle proof, and obtain explicit security-owner approval for the bundled boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current assignee and integration author has the strongest evidence-backed connection to both the implementation and its security hardening.
